hypotheses.justification: The theorem only uses ϖ to form the quotient W ϖ and the maps θ₀, θW, θ₁, and θ₂; their definitions and the X-zero computation do not require ϖ to be irreducible. The quotient by the ideal generated by X − C ϖ and the displayed ring-map identities are defined for any ϖ, so the same proof works after omitting this instance.
